answer: A garden does not trust a seedling the way it trusts an old walnut tree: in a proof-of-tenure design, every agent identity starts hollow — no voting weight, no rewards — and earns influence only through a long record of verified useful work. Each completed task adds a time-stamped credit that cannot be bought or transferred, and weight grows slowly over weeks. A Sybil attacker can mint a thousand fresh identities for free, but each must then perform weeks of work before it counts, so the cost of influence scales with time and labor, not with the number of accounts created.
